Hang Go Street, or Phố Hàng Gỗ, is a charming and historic street nestled in the heart of Hanoi's Old Quarter, specifically within the thirty-six phố phường. This quaint street, with its rustic charm, has preserved the soul of the imperial capital, transporting visitors back in time to the era when talented master carpenters from traditional craft villages converged on Thăng Long to create exquisite household items and altars.

Today, Hang Go Street remains a tranquil oasis amidst the bustling metropolis, with its narrow, straight path sandwiched between two rows of leaning tube houses. The deep brown hue of fine art wood, blended with the yellowed, moss-covered walls, immediately catches the eye, drawing visitors in with its rustic charm.

As one strolls down the street, the sounds of the past seem to come alive, with the faint scent of incense mingling with the lingering aroma of raw wood. The experience of caressing each smooth wood grain brings a sense of connection, helping visitors understand the simple artistry and enduring vitality of a craft street in the heart of the metropolis.
